restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224); total work over all processors, including a charged budget of 2,304 thread-hours (2^46.865 units) for the published characteristic search, whose time is not published. Grouped first-block evaluation (L = 2^16 trials sharing W0..W14, W15 = r15 + j) reduces main-loop work A to 2^44.611 units and total time to 2^47.198 < 2^47.25 units (ungrouped full-compression total is 2^47.385 < 2^47.39).

Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes; complete SHA-256 with standard IV, steps 0..31 on all three padded blocks, feed-forward and all 256 digest bits; outputs are verified by full recomputation.

Derived (not published) 32-step truncation of the 35-step attack of Li, Liu, Wang, Shi (CRYPTO 2026, ePrint 2026/1080); uses its Fig. 6 characteristic and starting solution as advice whose search costs are charged. No published complexity for an ordinary 32-step collision is known to us.

Heuristic bound: relies on the declared heuristics q-32step-matching-rate (analytic table prediction plus own measurements), step3-46-conditions and trail-search-budget; a verified 128-byte 32-step colliding message pair (digest f8a3db111360e5ed2e63041ecfa82b01c95a25882910bc0f21671949296a4e77) from an executed run of this 32-step truncated characteristic is attached as certificate sha256-r32-record-witness.
One run with T = 2^45.3 trials and at most 2^28.4 Step-3 invocations; no restarts; the precomputed table is built in place (no auxiliary sort buffer).

heuristics.statement: A uniformly random first block M0, compressed with the 32-step compression from the standard IV, yields at least 2^-17.36 expected valid tuples (Step 2 of proof.md Section 6) against the precomputed table TAB2 of 1,396,774,912 tuples.
heuristics.scope: The exact TAB2 and Step-2 test defined in proof.md Section 6 and Appendix A, with C_32 first blocks.
heuristics.extrapolation: Analytic prediction 2^-17.3254 from an exact enumeration of TAB2 combined with the structure of the Step-2 equations (each test's predicted pass fraction matches its measured fraction), assuming the CV1 words of C_32(IV, M0) behave as uniform for these tests; four measurement runs (2^35.2 part-trials, 62,179 valid tuples) give a pooled 2^-17.3337 with 99% lower bound 2^-17.3476. Extrapolated to the attack's fresh random coins and 2^45.3 trials.
heuristics.limitations: The enumeration and the measurements were run with our own C code (predicates given as inert source in Appendix A), not executed by the organizer. The prediction treats the W21 sign pattern as independent of the W6/E2 conditioning. Fallback evidence regime: the source paper's published 35-step rate 2^-20.92 would give a total of 2^49.28 (proof.md Section 9); the scored claim uses 2^-17.36.

heuristics.statement: For a valid tuple, each of the 196,608 (W14,W15) candidates follows the characteristic through step 22 and W16..W31 with probability at least 2^-46 (45 printed conditions plus the necessary unprinted condition E16[29] = E17[29]), and Step 3 succeeds with probability r >= 2^-28.415 * (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: Steps 16..22 and expanded words W16..W31 of the second block, conditional on Steps 1-2 and the P4 list of proof.md Section 6. Candidates of one tuple share W14 in 12 groups of 2^14, and the 12 W20 conditions are common to a group; this is charged in the second-moment bound of proof.md Section 8.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured cumulative rates through steps 16-21 over 2^33.5 candidates (2^-3.000, 2^-14.999, 2^-21.002, 2^-28.15, 2^-31.19, 2^-31.51) agree with the stage-by-stage condition mapping (predicted 2^-3, 2^-15, 2^-21, 2^-28, 2^-32, 2^-33); the 13 conditions after step 21 are extrapolated from the printed count, with a Monte Carlo on the published pair's tuple giving about 2^-11 for them.
heuristics.limitations: Independence among conditions and among candidates beyond the W14 grouping is not proved; no full conformance was observed at our sample size; the post-step-21 Monte Carlo used one tuple's (W6, W7, W8) differences; measurements are our own code.

heuristics.statement: The SAT/SMT searches that produced the 35-step characteristic of the source paper (Sect. 3 Model-1/2/3 and Sect. 4 Steps 1-4) cost at most 2,304 thread-hours, charged as 2^57.98 word operations = 2^46.865 target-compression units.
heuristics.scope: Eight minimisation tasks described in ePrint 2026/1080 (Model-1, Model-2 in two phases, Model-3, Steps 1-4), each charged 288 thread-hours (four solver calls at a 72-hour cap on one thread), converted at 2^35 word operations per thread-second, charged once as preprocessing.
heuristics.extrapolation: No search time is published. The 72-hour per-call limit is the example limit stated by the same first three authors for the same tool family (ePrint 2024/349, Sect. 4.3); the number of calls per task is our assumption. The conversion is above the hardware peak of the source paper's server (at most 2^34.82 instructions per thread-second).
heuristics.limitations: Unverified budget: the number of calls per task and threads per call are not published. A larger true search cost raises the score: 4,608 thread-hours (or conversion at 2^36) gives 2^48.15 total, 9,216 thread-hours 2^49.01 (sensitivity table in proof.md Section 9).

heuristics.statement: Producing the starting solution T (A4..A13, E8..E13, W12, W13) costs the source paper's reported Step-1 time 2^34.3, charged here as 2^35 units.
heuristics.scope: The advice values listed in proof.md Section 6.
heuristics.extrapolation: The paper does not state the unit of 2^34.3; the charged 2^35 covers a 35-step-compression unit.
heuristics.limitations: The values are read from the published pair, which arose from the paper's single solution; the paper's SAT time is not independently reproduced. Its contribution to the total is below 2^-12 relative.
